title: The Missing Sector
logline: An eccentric scientist discovers that historical star charts have been deliberately shifted to hide a masked sector, but a nervous inspector is desperately trying to erase their findings before the truth causes widespread panic.

roles.description: Brilliant but entirely lacking in social grace, obsessed with orbital mechanics.
Tasked with maintaining the official registry, terrified of what the missing data implies.
The bureaucratic body that officially certifies all celestial discoveries.
A dark, sensor-baffled region of the local debris field.
A heavy, unmarked corporate suppression vessel.
A massive data vault holding centuries of unaltered astronomical records.
A cluttered orbital observatory filled with physical star charts.

public_situation: The {role:research_institute} has publicly disavowed the work of the {role:obsessive_scientist}, claiming their recent celestial measurements are the result of faulty equipment.
private_truth: The scientist is right: a massive chunk of local space was scrubbed from the databases fifty years ago, and the inspector has been ordered to ensure it stays that way.

beats.public_change: The scientist is locked out of their own lab and broadcasts a desperate plea for help.

missions.reason: The scientist needs the pilot to break the quarantine seal on their lab and extract their primary hard drive.
missions.private_fact: The drive contains the only uncorrupted copy of the true star charts.

missions.reason: The inspector hires the pilot to scan the lab's exterior for unauthorized data transmissions.
missions.private_fact: The inspector is just trying to pinpoint the scientist's physical location.

beats.public_change: The inspector issues a system-wide warrant for the scientist's arrest on charges of data terrorism.

missions.reason: The pilot must travel to the neighbouring system and manually deliver the hard drive into the archive's deep storage to preserve it.
missions.private_fact: The scientist knows the inspector cannot legally wipe the deep storage without a tribunal.

missions.reason: The inspector, panicking, hires the pilot to destroy an automated guard ship hunting the scientist.
missions.private_fact: The cruiser belongs to the inspector's own superiors, who are coming to clean up the mess.

beats.public_change: The institute goes into total lockdown, halting all astronomical research.

missions.reason: The institute is moving the scientist's backup tapes on a secure transport. The pilot must blow out the transport and recover them.
missions.private_fact: The tapes contain the exact coordinates of the missing sector.

missions.reason: The pilot must fly to the unmapped coordinates and scan the sector to prove it exists.
missions.private_fact: The sector is filled with the wreckage of an old, undocumented corporate war.

beats.public_change: The pilot returns with proof of the missing system, but the inspector is waiting for them.

missions.reason: The scientist pays the pilot to destroy the final corporate suppression cruiser blocking their broadcast array.
missions.private_fact: The inspector hails the pilot, offering to expunge their criminal record and pay a massive bounty if they hand over the proof instead.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot fights off the suppression ship and broadcasts the coordinates.
resolutions.summary: The truth about the missing sector breaks the institute's authority. The scientist is hailed as a visionary, and the inspector is fired.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot proved the local star charts were a lie and found a whole masked sector hiding in the dark.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot takes the inspector's offer and hands over the proof.
resolutions.summary: The missing sector is scrubbed forever. The scientist is institutionalized for 'space madness', but the pilot gets rich.
The scientist is quietly disappeared by corporate suppression forces. The star charts remain a comforting lie.

loose_threads.detail: The digital signature on the forged star charts belongs to a retired mining surveyor who officially died twenty years before the edits were made.
The inspector nervously mentions that the institute's funding relies entirely on 'stability clauses' from an unknown benefactor.

radio_hooks: {role:research_institute} issues reminder that independent orbital measurements are highly inaccurate.
Local astronomy enthusiast claims entire constellation is 'missing'; experts blame cheap telescopes.

voice_direction.obsessive_scientist: Fast, breathless, constantly interrupts themselves with new thoughts.
voice_direction.nervous_inspector: Quiet, precise, hesitates frequently before starting sentences.
